org.name: Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

hazard: Absence of mental health liaison attendance during 72‑hour hold
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Aaron Deeley: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: In order to strengthen collaborative working across the two Trusts, a project group for development of the 'joint protocol' is being put into place. The first meeting with attendees from both Trusts has been arranged for 23rd September 2024

concerns.quote: Patients admitted onto a ward at the acute Trust detained under various sections of the Mental Health Act have an allocated Responsible Clinician. As section 5 (2) is a holding power only, there is no Responsible Clinician allocated for a vulnerable patient being held pending assessment for consideration for detention under the Mental health Act
concerns.hazard: lack of assigned responsible clinician for patients held under section 5(2)

concerns.quote: During the waiting period of up to 72 hours, Mental Health Liaison will not attend the acute ward or make assessment of the presenting risks of self-harm
concerns.hazard: absence of mental health liaison attendance during 72‑hour hold

concerns.quote: The acute care healthcare professionals do not have specialist mental health training to conduct a mental health assessment and the consequential presenting harm
concerns.hazard: untrained staff conducting mental health assessment

concerns.quote: There was confusion at the acute Trust as to what regime was required to ensure that a patient awaiting Mental Health Act assessment could be put under 1:1 observation. The Trust policy was confusing and did not cover patients like Aaron Deeley
concerns.hazard: confusing policy on 1:1 observation for detained patients

concerns.quote: There is no joint protocol to cover the working between the two Trusts on this issue as the referral for Mental Health Act assessment goes outside of both organisations
concerns.hazard: absence of joint protocol between trusts

concerns.quote: There is a lacuna for patients awaiting Mental Health Act assessment and requiring simultaneous physical healthcare when a significant risk has been identified such that a patient may require detention for their own safety
concerns.hazard: gap in care for patients needing both physical and mental health services

reports.title: Nicholas Gray: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: The Trust PSIRF Decision Monitoring Tool completed after Mr Gray died contained inaccurate information, the dates of EPUT contact and the substance of the interactions were inaccurate
concerns.hazard: inaccurate information in PSIRF Decision Monitoring Tool

concerns.quote: Self-harm was noted as "none known or recorded
There was no record of the mental health liaison nurse review on 24 June 2023 and the discharge of Mr Gray from EPUT
concerns.hazard: missing mental health liaison nurse review and discharge record

concerns.quote: The information used to inform a potential investigation requirement contained significant omissions and was not consistent with the information known to the Trust

links.explanation: Both concerns involve the absence or inadequacy of mental health liaison involvement/records for patients needing assessment. The earlier report notes a gap in liaison attendance during up to 72‑hour waits, while the later report highlights a missing record of a liaison nurse review on a specific date.
